The first excerpt from Dickens describes the contradictory nature of the French Revolution era, while the second from Wordsworth expresses the initial optimism it inspired.  
Both reflect the influence of Enlightenment ideas—such as liberty, reason, and challenging traditional authority—that underpinned the revolutionary movements of the late 18th century.  
The Reformation (A) was a 16th-century religious movement; mercantilism (B) was an economic policy; the Reconquista (D) was a medieval campaign in Iberia. Only the Enlightenment (C) fits as the intellectual foundation of these revolutions.  

Final answer: (C)
